Maladaptive Strategies.value: Driving or being a passenger in a vehicle
Being in circumstances that remind me of the event (eg, being in the dark).

Threat.value: I only feel safe in a very limited number of places
I constantly scan my surroundings for signs of danger
I jump or startle at ordinary sounds that would not bother most people

Memory.value: When I remember the frightening event I feel like it is happening right now.
I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind.
Fragments of the memory appear suddenly without warning and then disappear

Negative Appraisals.value: If I think about the event, I will not be able to handle it
My life has been destroyed by the trauma
I can't stop bad things from happening to me

issues.explanation: For a life-threatening motor vehicle collision, helicopter/aircraft sounds are not impossible but are hard to reconcile here because no other items suggest air transport, emergency airlift, or trauma cues involving aircraft; the rest of the profile is road-collision focused only in a very general way. This trigger therefore stands out as weakly anchored to the trauma and to the rest of the selected items.

issues.item: Avoid Night: Going out at night or being outside after dark
issues.explanation: Avoiding going out at night is difficult to link specifically to the reported motor vehicle collision given the rest of the profile. There are no corresponding night-time triggers, darkness-related threat beliefs, or memory items suggesting the trauma was tied to night conditions, so this strategy appears to address a symptom pattern not represented elsewhere.

issues.item: Threat in Silence: Unusual silence makes me feel something dangerous is about to happen
issues.explanation: Feeling danger in unusual silence is not impossible, but it fits poorly with the listed triggers and trauma context. The trigger set includes bus riding, criticism, and helicopter sounds rather than quiet/silence cues, so this threat item is not well connected to the rest of the formulation for this profile.

issues.item: Triggers: Being Criticised: Being criticised or corrected
issues.explanation: Being criticised or corrected is difficult to link clinically to a life-threatening motor vehicle collision when the rest of the profile is dominated by transport/noise/intrusive re-experiencing themes. It stands apart from the accident-related trigger pattern and is not supported by corresponding memory or threat content.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Character Blame: The event happened to me because of the sort of person I am
issues.explanation: Character-based self-blame is possible after trauma, but here it is weakly grounded in the rest of the profile. The other items center on fear, helplessness, and destroyed life rather than a coherent trauma-specific belief about personal defect causing a motor vehicle collision. This makes the appraisal set feel internally mixed.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Relaxation: avoid relaxing because it feels dangerous
issues.explanation: Avoiding relaxation because it feels dangerous is not impossible in PTSD, but in this profile it is poorly connected to the other selected items, which focus on vehicle-related triggers, intrusive sensory memories, and situational danger monitoring. It suggests a generalized arousal-management pattern that is not otherwise represented strongly enough in the profile.
